paras: Sceloporus mucronatus, also known commonly as the cleft lizard, the central cleft lizard, and la espinosa mucronada in Mexican Spanish, is a species of lizard in the subfamily Sceloporinae of the family Phrynosomatidae. The species is endemic to Mexico. There are two recognized subspecies.
Sceloporus mucronatus is found in the Mexican states of Guerrero, Hidalgo, Oaxaca, Puebla, and Veracruz, and in Mexico City.

The preferred natural habitats of Sceloporus mucronatus are forest and shrubland, at elevations of 2,000–3,700 m (6,600–12,100 ft), but it has also been found in agricultural areas, where it shelters in rock crevices.
Sceloporus mucronatus gives birth to live young. Its mode of reproduction has been described as viviparous and as ovoviviparous.
Two subspecies of Sceloporus mucronatus are recognized as being valid, including the nominotypical subspecies.
Sceloporus mucronatus olsoni Webb, Lemos-Espinal & H.M. Smith, 2002
The subspecific name, olsoni, is in honor of American herpetologist Rupert Earl Olson.
